0.original: Little does Nidhana know that she is about to send you on another errand.

26.original: Gather information at the tower outpost.

29.original: Ride the hamsa to the Giantsgall Grounds.

48.original: If you will excuse me, I shall return to my work on the talisman.

49.original: Ah, you are both back. Excellent.

50.original: I have a message for you, Mistress Nidhana.

51.original: It would seem the stores of giantsgall are running low.

52.original: What? But when last I looked, there was still plenty...

53.original: I suspect that was before Urianger told everyone about their tempering cure, and Estinien shared his knowledge of dragons. Your peers have since been inspired to fashion a number of new talisman prototypes.

54.original: I see... Well, if it leads to new possibilities, then far be it from me to complain, but we will need to replenish our stores...

55.original: I should be happy to tend to this if you like.

56.original: As much as I appreciate the offer, my dear boy, I can't in good conscience send you out there alone while kidnappers are at large.

57.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>─loath though I am to press another task on you so soon, might I ask you to fetch the giantsgall?

58.original: In case you're not familiar, giantsgall is a type of ore found on the island. Owing to its hardness and aetherial conductivity, it has applications in many disciplines─alchemy not least of all.

59.original: The quarry where it is found, aptly named Giantsgall Grounds, isn't far away, so it shouldn't take much of your time. May we impose on you once more?

60.original: Thank you! Upon arriving at the grounds, please seek out a man named Zeynuha. He will furnish you with the ore.

61.original: At the very least, permit me to accompany you. It so happens I have an errand of my own that will take me to the outpost nearby.

62.original: May we borrow a pair of hamsa, Mistress Nidhana?

63.original: By all means. Do try to be patient with them─those that survived are still in training.

64.original: I will bring the hamsa to the entrance. Meet me there when you are ready.

65.original: Despite his tender years, Varshahn is thoughtful and dependable. It's easy to see why he was chosen to be the satrap's attendant!

66.original: Here are our hamsa, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. If the creatures look familiar, it is because they are close kin to your Eorzean dodos.

67.original: Hamsa have long been kept as livestock in Thavnair, and many a hatchery may be found here. Alas, the largest of these was recently razed by monsters from the tower.

68.original: On account of said hatchery being situated near the tower, the Radiant Host repurposed its remnants as an outpost.

69.original: That is where my errand takes me, and your own destination is but a stone's throw away.

70.original: If you have no objections, let us first make for the outpost. We set forth at your word.

71.original: You are ready? Then let us depart. You need only ride and relax─my bird and I will take the lead for yours to follow.

72.original: Mount the hamsa and travel to the outpost?

73.original: Let us be off. If you haven't ridden dodos before, be warned that they have a wobbling gait.

74.original: That spectacular formation stretching out over the water is called Khadga─a word which means “sword.”

75.original: This sword, legend holds, was wielded by the Manusya against the Mrga before it was cast down at conflict's end.

76.original: To the left and requiring no introduction is the tower. As you can see, it straddles a small isle.

77.original: Almost there. Though the main part of the hatchery is atop the cliff, the outpost itself is on the beach.

78.original: And here we are. Manned by the Radiant Host, this outpost is our first line of defense against the tower.

79.original: Well, well, who should it be but young Varshahn. On an errand for the satrap?

80.original: I am. His Excellency bade me come to collect your report.

81.original: He also wished to express his heartfelt gratitude to the brave men and women of the Radiant Host for their unflagging dedication.

82.original: We simply do our duty, but we are honored to receive His Excellency's regard.

83.original: And yet, for his boundless benevolence, his treatment of one so young could be regarded as...callous.

84.original: Though we have enjoyed relative peace and calm these past few days, this remains the front line of battle. No place for children.

85.original: Your predecessor too often traveled alone. It's been, what, two years now since you took over? I wonder how the fellow is faring...

86.original: Like those before him, he went on to represent the satrap in foreign lands. Wherever he may now be, I am certain he is well.

87.original: As for myself, I assure you that all I do, I do of my own volition, and gladly. I pray you do not think ill of His Excellency.

88.original: Certainly not, lad... Whatever happens, my faith in the satrap is unwavering. But still I worry for you.

89.original: We would be overcome with sadness if something were to befall you, for you are as a little brother to us all. Take care, do you hear?

91.original: And who might this be? Not Hannish by the look of <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468696D03>.

92.original: Permit me to introduce <hex:022903EB0203>, of the Eorzean contingent, come to assist in the making of the talisman.

93.original: From Eorzea, you say! Towers have appeared over there too, yes? Tell me, what is the situation like?

94.original: May I suggest that you exchange information with our soldiers? Both parties would stand to learn something of value, I believe.

95.original: An excellent idea. Given the unprecedented nature of the threat, some of ours are understandably anxious. We would be glad for any tidings you can share.

96.original: You two, bring Varshahn the latest report, and answer any questions he may have.

97.original: All appears quiet with the tower at the moment. I daresay the soldiers won't mind if you approached them.

98.original: The last monster that came out of the tower laid waste to the hatchery, slaughtering many good hamsa. The poor creatures didn't deserve it...

99.original: This is the fellow that carried you hither. Its breathing is somewhat ragged, perhaps due to its inexperience as a mount.

100.original: It occurs to me I have yet to properly introduce our company.

101.original: We are the Radiant Host, a military order under the satrap's command. Our duty is to preserve peace in the land, be it patrolling the streets or dealing with heretofore unknown threats such as now.

102.original: We train hard, and admit only capable warriors to our ranks. Even so, we've struggled to contend with the fiends from the tower.

103.original: Though we succeeded in striking them down on the two occasions they came in force, we had to pay a heavy price.

104.original: What of the towers in Eorzea? Do they likewise spawn monsters?

105.original: So it's much the same everywhere... With every nation struggling, we cannot expect calls for outside aid to be answered.

106.original: My thanks not only for the information, but for accompanying Varshahn besides. While he's wise beyond his years, he's still a child, and we couldn't bear to see him come to harm.

107.original: You wish to know about the tower? To be honest, we know little and less about it ourselves.

108.original: This “Tower of Zot,” as folk have taken to calling it, suddenly appeared where it did on the isle of Narunnair.

109.original: We're safe from its influence at this distance, but go too far into the water, and you'll expose yourself to its corrupting aether.

110.original: You're a foreigner, aren't you? How are they dealing with the tower in your homeland?

111.original: Our struggles are not unique... Then our hopes still lie with the talismans. We must keep the monsters contained until they're ready.

112.original: When the tower first appeared, we sent scouts on a boat to investigate. But it quickly became apparent that something was amiss.

113.original: One after another our comrades were corrupted. We could only look on in horror as they slew each other...

114.original: Ah, I've heard about you. The visitor from Eorzea. Is there anything you can tell us about the Telophoroi?

115.original: We know that they're the ones behind the tower, and that they've declared war on the whole world.

116.original: But why are they doing this? What is it that they want? This, we don't understand.

117.original: ...What? They want to die...and take everyone with them!? What madness is this!?

118.original: Well, you can bet that we won't let those bastards have their way! We'll fight them with everything we have, like our Eorzean and Far Eastern brothers!

119.original: Grrr, those demented fools... If they want to go to hell, they can bloody well arrange their own passage, and leave the rest of us out of it!

120.original: Finished speaking with the soldiers, have you? I hope it was as enlightening for you as it was for them.

121.original: As a neutral nation and trading hub both, Radz<hex:021F0103>at<hex:021F0103>Han ordinarily receives a steady stream of news from abroad. Alas, this stream dried up when trading vessels stopped coming.

122.original: Amidst the dearth of information, everyone will have been grateful for your account.

123.original: ...But come, you had best see to your original errand. As mine will keep me here awhile longer, however, I'm afraid I cannot guide you the rest of the way.

124.original: Worry not, the path is straightforward─you need but follow the road east. Upon the hamsa, you will arrive before you know it.

125.original: Brief though it was, I enjoyed our time together. Till we meet again.

126.original: Lest you have forgotten, to get to the Giantsgall Grounds, you need but follow the road east. The hamsa should deliver you there quite quickly.

127.original: Though the hamsa appears to want to return home, it reluctantly offers you its back.

128.original: Should you become separated from your steed, speak with the Radiant beastkeeper at the Hamsa Hatchery to mount it again.

130.original: If you're looking for your hamsa, it returned here by itself a while ago. You still have need of it?

131.original: No sooner do you arrive at your destination than the hamsa dashes off...

132.original: Speak with the Radiant beastkeeper at the Hamsa Hatchery to mount the hamsa, then ride it to the Giantsgall Grounds.

133.original: Aye, this is indeed the Giantsgall Grounds, and I am Zeynuha. Is there something you require?

134.original: Giantsgall for the alchemists, you say? But of course they shall have it!

135.original: They labor tirelessly to deal with the tower, and 'tis the least we can do to provide them with the materials they need.
